title: Mothers of the believers
hook: the Prophet's wives are called mothers of the believers (33:6)
tomorrow: Men and women, side by side

segments.voice: Yesterday, uswah, and your line was a beautiful example. Which small sunnah did you copy, and when? Day five hundred forty.

Ask a Muslim child the names of the Prophet's daughters, or his wives, and many will know Khadijah and 'A'isha at least. Many Muslim parents name their daughters after them. In many mosques and books, each of the wives is mentioned with a short phrase of honor after her name: may God be pleased with her. And the Qur'an itself gives them, together, a title that turns a household into a family for a whole community. It's in Surah Al-Ahzab.

Pickthall: "The Prophet is closer to the believers than their selves, and his wives are (as) their mothers." Ummahat al-mu'minin: the mothers of the believers. The title meant honor and respect. It also meant, as the same surah says later, that no one could marry them after the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. Mothers to a whole community. Who were they? Historians usually list eleven women who were married to him at different times. Khadijah first, a widow and a successful merchant, older than him, his only wife for about twenty-five years, the first person to believe in his message. Sawdah, a widow who had emigrated to Abyssinia. 'A'isha, daughter of Abu Bakr, who became one of the great teachers of the early community; thousands of hadith come through her. Hafsah, daughter of 'Umar, who kept a written copy of the Qur'an. Zaynab bint Khuzaymah, called the mother of the poor for her charity. Umm Salamah, whose advice at Hudaybiyyah helped calm a crisis. Zaynab bint Jahsh, known for working with her hands and giving the money away. Juwayriyah, Umm Habibah, Safiyyah and Maymunah. Many were widows. Several came from families or tribes that had been at war with the Muslims. Some marriages were alliances, some acts of protection, some, the sources say plainly, of love. Sunni and Shia Muslims both use the title, and both honor Khadijah deeply; they differ in how they view some of the wives' roles in the conflicts after the Prophet's death. What the verse gives is a family. Every believer, it says, has mothers, and knows their names.

segments.voice: Here's the practice: learn one of their names. Sit, and let the breath settle. Of the names you just heard, which one stayed with you? Khadijah, the first to believe. 'A'isha, the teacher. Hafsah, who kept the pages. Zaynab, mother of the poor. Umm Salamah, the adviser. Pick one. Say her name slowly. Decide to look up one more fact about her today, from a good source. Think of what she might teach someone living now. If you pray, you can ask God to be pleased with her. The bell holds the time.
Mothers of the believers. Ummahat al-mu'minin: the title Al-Ahzab gives the Prophet's wives, honored as mothers of the whole community. Today's word.
Your line: mothers of the believers. Today, tell someone one thing you learned about the mother of the believers you chose. Day five hundred forty.

fork.setup: the Qur'an gives the Prophet's wives a title. what does it make them to every believer?
fork.reveal: 33:6: his wives are as their mothers, ummahat al-mu'minin.

original.note: Arabic: the mothers of the believers, the title of the Prophet's wives from 33:6.

trapdoor: what you thought: an honorary title for the Prophet's wives.
what it means: a community given mothers, women whose names Muslims learn: merchants, teachers, givers and advisers.
what a scholar hears: 33:6's ummahatuhum, with 33:53 on not marrying them after him; eleven wives in most lists; and Sunni and Shia differences over some later roles.

notes: Pickthall 33:6 quoted from memory; confirm wording.
The list of eleven wives follows the usual Sunni list; status of Mariya al-Qibtiyya and Rayhana is discussed by scholars; neither is named. Confirm.

Biographical details (Sawdah's emigration to Abyssinia, Hafsah's copy of the Qur'an, Zaynab bint Khuzaymah 'mother of the poor', Umm Salamah's advice at Hudaybiyyah, Zaynab bint Jahsh's handwork and charity) are from sira and hadith; confirm each.
Khadijah 'older than him' and 'about twenty-five years' of monogamous marriage: common figures; confirm.
